entries.title: Judges 8:1
segments: Those who neglect their duty are often disposed to cast the blame on others; and those who refuse to engage in great and important services, are often most anxious to have the credit of them.

entries.title: Judges 8:2
segments: The gleaning--the vintage; Gideon, of the house of Abi-ezer, and his men, who had struck the first blow, are compared to those who gather the vintage; while the Ephraimites, who came after him, are compared to gleaners.  But here Gideon tells them that the gleaning of the grapes is more than the original vintage.  This was a soft answer, designed to appease the wrath of the Ephraimites.
A command of one's temper, and a disposition to give full credit to the worthy actions of others, are likely means of appeasing envy, abating wrath, and causing contentions to cease.

entries.title: Judges 8:5
segments: Succoth; a city in the tribe of Gad, on the east of Jordan, below the sea of Galilee.

entries.title: Judges 8:6
segments: Now in thy hand; have you already taken them?

They were men of worldly prudence, but without either faith in God or devotion to his cause; and would not assist Gideon till they were first sure of his success. 
 
It is unwise to refuse aid to brethren in distress, and foolish as well as wicked to upbraid them.

entries.title: Judges 8:7
segments: Tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness; a mode of punishment not uncommon in those days.

entries.title: Judges 8:8
segments: Penuel; east of Succoth, and near the river Jabbok.

entries.title: Judges 8:9
segments: This tower; one to which the men of Penuel trusted for their defence.

entries.title: Judges 8:10
segments:
Karkor; supposed to have been eastward of Penuel, and near the borders of Gad. 
 
The multitudes who have fallen in wars by the hands of their fellow men, and in the indulgence of the most hateful passions, present an impressive view of the evil of sin, and of the horrible state of those who are abandoned to its everlasting power.

entries.title: Judges 8:11
segments:
Nobah is the same as Kenath, and is supposed to be the same as the modern Kanatha in Hauran. 
 
  Jogbehah was in its neighborhood.

entries.title: Judges 8:14
segments: Described unto him; literally, wrote for him; probably gave him their names.

entries.title: Judges 8:16
segments:
Taught the men; showed them the folly of their course by punishing them. 
 
Sin often brings misery in this world of mercy, as it will, to all who continue in it, in the world of retribution.

entries.title: Judges 8:21
segments:
So is his strength; as his age was mature, so was his strength. 
 
The dread which men have of a lingering and dishonorable temporal death, should prompt them to immediate, earnest, and persevering efforts to avoid the disgrace and torment of that which is eternal.

entries.title: Judges 8:23
segments:
The Lord shall rule; he was their chief magistrate, and Gideon would not be instrumental in changing that form of government. 
 
A wise man will not covet an increase of power, care, and responsibility; nor, unless it appears to be manifestly the will of God, will he consent to receive it.

entries.title: Judges 8:24
segments:
Ear-rings of his prey; those which they had taken from their enemies. 
 
  Ishmaelites; the Midianites are sometimes confounded with Ishmaelites; they lived near, and often mingled together.

entries.title: Judges 8:27
segments: An ephod; a very rich and costly garment, such as was worn by the high-priest.

A whoring after it; it became a means of superstition and idolatry. 
 
The consequences of men's actions may be very different from what they anticipate; they should not, therefore, at any time lean to their own understandings, but should in all their ways acknowledge God, that he may direct their paths.

entries.title: Judges 8:31
segments: A departure from the design and will of God in the institution of marriage, has in some form ever been the easily besetting sin of men, and the source of innumerable and most distressing calamities.

entries.title: Judges 8:33
segments:
Baalim and--Baal-berith; idol-gods. 
 
No sooner are restraints removed, than men show their wickedness by voluntarily engaging in known sin, and the manifestation of awful ingratitude towards both God and men.
